audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer had Aurora winning all seven stages of a 50.0% matchup, while the full layer's own sides already read Akshan for levels 1 through 5 and Skill afterwards. Every one of those four early rows also carried a 'why' describing Aurora winning the stage.
audit.why: Avengerang is 850 range on 9s at rank 1 and extends its range every time it hits an enemy, so the minion wave lengthens his poke instead of shielding you from it; his passive adds a second attack and a shield on every third hit. That is an early-game edge, not a deficit.
audit.corrected: Akshan levels 1-5, Skill from 6 on. content win[] moved onto the full layer's sides and the four contradicting whys rewritten to state why he wins them.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit Q/P text, ranges and cooldowns)

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was written as 'Between Worlds phases you clean through the missile' — Aurora's R has no phase, no untargetability and no missile-dodge. Riot gives it a leap, a shockwave, a slow zone and a cross-zone teleport.
audit.why: A player told the ult dodges Comeuppance will ult into it and die at 2500 range.
audit.corrected: Comeuppance's real spike is that it stores bullets and stops on the first champion, minion or structure hit, and its damage scales with missing health — the answer is a body in the path, not a dodge.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief ownerKit R text, enemyKit R text)

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions were absent from the whole matchup. (a) Dirty Fighting shields him on every third hit from attacks and abilities against a champion. (b) Avengerang extends its range each time it hits an enemy, so a minion wave makes it longer, not safer. (c) Heroic Swing fires a hook into TERRAIN and he is knocked off when he collides with champions or terrain — in open lane it has nothing to anchor to.
audit.why: The terrain requirement is the single fact that makes 'is Heroic Swing down?' answerable by positioning rather than by counting, and the shield is why burst has to arrive in one window rather than in pieces.
audit.corrected: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1, 800 range, and must anchor into terrain — fight in the open and it does nothing. Force the third-hit shield out with a Q before spending E. Do not treat the wave as cover from Avengerang.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no number at all.
audit.corrected: Heroic Swing 18s at rank 1, Avengerang 9s at rank 1 down to 5s at rank 5, Comeuppance 100s at rank 1, Going Rogue 18s at rank 1 down to 2s at rank 5.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Twin Drift' is not an Aurora ability; it appears in spikes[0].text and early.
audit.corrected: Both sentences describe the leap, which the full layer already names Across the Veil (W).
sources: existing breakdown.cooldowns names it 'W Across the Veil'

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t recommended anti-heal 'early into his sustain'. Akshan's kit has no heal — his passive grants a shield, which Grievous Wounds does not touch.
audit.why: An item slot spent on a mechanic the enemy does not have.
audit.corrected: Zhonya's is the item that matters: Comeuppance arrives as one burst.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit P flag is 'shield', no heal anywhere)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere mentioned Going Rogue: camouflage with a 5500-unit reach on 18s at rank 1 falling to 2s and free at rank 5.
audit.why: It is the entire reason his map presence changes after lane, and it is answered by a Control Ward, not by mobility.
audit.corrected: Sweep before you cross the river late; his roam window costs him nothing at rank 5.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit W range, cooldown, cost, stealth flag)

notes:
Level chart: content read Aurora on all seven rows while the full layer read Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Skill/Skill/Skill — two opposite answers rendered on the same page. Worse, all four Akshan-side rows carried a why describing Aurora winning that stage. I moved content win[] onto the full layer's sides as one atomic group and rewrote phases[0..3].why so the sentence agrees with the verdict above it. packet.levelChart still reads all-Aurora and disagrees with both layers.

Derived-flag misfire: Akshan's W and E both carry the 'terrain — creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' flag. Riot's text says neither creates terrain: the E hooks INTO existing terrain and the W is camouflage. I wrote the description's version — the swing needs a wall to anchor to — and asserted nothing about either creating terrain.

SuspectNames: 'Save Between Worlds' is a real ability name, so the near-miss flag is a false positive, but the line was wrong anyway — Between Worlds does not dodge Comeuppance and the actual answer is a minion in the path.

Unverified and left alone: whether Aurora's Across the Veil invisibility breaks Akshan's Comeuppance lock-on once it has been acquired. Riot's text says the ultimate locks onto an enemy champion and stores bullets, but says nothing about what breaks the lock, and the kit files carry no entry for it. I did not claim it in either direction.
